key_insight: K/Rb double perovskite halides β2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and highly tunable in bandgap, making them promising lead-free materials for photovoltaics, photodetectors, and thermoelectrics.
engineering_relevance: The chloride variants fit single-junction solar absorption, while bromide/iodide variants extend utility to tandem cells and near-IR devices, with the iodides also showing very high thermoelectric efficiency.
method: DFT-based structural, electronic, optical, mechanical, and thermoelectric screening
Evaluate formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor for stability
Analyze elastic constants, band structures, carrier masses, thermal conductivity, and ZT
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV, ductile elastic behavior across all compounds, and a peak ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: These are first-principles predictions, so experimental synthesis quality, phase purity, and defect tolerance will determine whether the reported performance is realized in devices.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
